title: Sixth Word Applying The Comparison Selling The Trust

questions.question: In the parable, who does the king stand for?
questions.answer: He stands for Allah, our Creator and Sustainer.

questions.question: What do the estates and tools in the parable stand for in a person's life?
questions.answer: They stand for a person's body, soul, heart, senses, and other things Allah has given.

questions.question: Who is represented by the noble lieutenant?
questions.answer: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings be upon him.

questions.question: What does the wise decree stand for?
questions.answer: It stands for the Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the battlefield picture show about this world?
questions.answer: It shows that this world keeps changing and nothing stays forever.

questions.question: What question do people begin to ask when they see things passing away?
questions.answer: They wonder if there is a way to keep what they have from being lost forever.

questions.question: What answer does the Qur’an give to that worry?
questions.answer: It says there is a good and easy way.

questions.question: What is that way?
questions.answer: It is to give back the trust to its real Owner by dedicating oneself and one’s belongings to Allah.

questions.question: Why is this called a trust?
questions.answer: Because what people have really belongs to Allah and is only placed with them for a time.

questions.question: What kind of result comes from this trade?
questions.answer: It brings five kinds of benefit.

questions.question: What is the main lesson of the parable explained in this passage?
questions.answer: A person should offer himself and what he has to Allah, because Allah is the true Owner.

questions.question: Which parts of a person are included among the trusts from Allah?
questions.answer: The body, spirit, heart, eyes, tongue, mind, imagination, and other inner and outer abilities.

questions.question: Why is the world compared to a battlefield?
questions.answer: Because it is full of change, loss, and uncertainty.

questions.question: What feeling does the changing world create in people?
questions.answer: It makes them realize that things slip away and do not last.

questions.question: According to the passage, where does the true solution come from?
questions.answer: It comes from the Qur’an.

questions.question: What does it mean to sell the trust back to its true Owner?
questions.answer: It means using your life and gifts the way Allah wants.

questions.question: Is this trade shown as harmful or beneficial?
questions.answer: It is shown as very beneficial.

questions.question: How many benefits are mentioned for making this trade?
questions.answer: Five benefits.

questions.question: How does the passage help the reader understand the parable?
questions.answer: It explains what each part of the story means in real life.

questions.question: In the explanation, who is being addressed by the words to the nafs?
questions.answer: A person’s selfish side that follows desires.

questions.question: What are some examples of outward and inward senses named in the passage?
questions.answer: The eye, the tongue, the mind, and the imagination.

questions.question: What role does the Messenger of Allah have in the explained parable?
questions.answer: He is the honored messenger who brings the message from Allah.

questions.question: What is the verse about in simple words?
questions.answer: It teaches that believers give themselves and their wealth to Allah and receive Paradise.

questions.question: What does the world’s constant changing show about earthly things?
questions.answer: It shows that worldly things are not permanent.

questions.question: According to the passage, who is the real owner of the trust?
questions.answer: Allah is the real Owner.

questions.question: What does the king’s title teach us about Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah rules forever, with no beginning and no end.

questions.question: What does it mean that our possessions are in life’s care only for a time?
questions.answer: It means we do not own them forever and cannot keep them permanently.

questions.question: Why are the body and senses included among possessions?
questions.answer: Because they are gifts given to us to use during our lives.

questions.question: Why is the Qur’an connected with the decree in the story?
questions.answer: Because it gives Allah’s guidance and shows the right path.

questions.question: What causes people to think deeply in the changing world?
questions.answer: Seeing everything fade, break apart, or pass away.

questions.question: What hope is offered after that worry?
questions.answer: There is a way to turn temporary things into lasting reward.

questions.question: What action begins that transformation?
questions.answer: Returning the trust to Allah by living for Him.

questions.question: What does the phrase true Owner teach about human ownership?
questions.answer: It teaches that human ownership is limited and temporary.

questions.question: What is the verse’s promise to believers in this passage?
questions.answer: If they give themselves and their wealth to Allah, they gain Paradise.

questions.question: How is the Qur’an described in relation to this trade?
questions.answer: It is described as the guide that explains it.

questions.question: What human problem is described by the image of things slipping from our hands?
questions.answer: People cannot stop worldly things from passing away.

questions.question: What does the passage say a person hears during that moment of worry?
questions.answer: The message of the Qur’an calling to an easy and beautiful way.

questions.question: What is being traded in this passage?
questions.answer: A person’s self and possessions are being offered to Allah.

questions.question: Why is giving them to Allah not a real loss?
questions.answer: Because Allah is their real Owner and gives great reward in return.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest about the value of worldly things by themselves?
questions.answer: By themselves, they do not last and cannot be fully kept.

questions.question: What does the phrase telescope of this parable suggest?
questions.answer: It suggests that the story helps us see the truth more clearly.

questions.question: Which two special roles of Allah are named when the king is explained?
questions.answer: Allah is described as the Sustainer and the Creator.

questions.question: Name two inner or outer abilities listed among Allah’s trusts.
questions.answer: Two examples are the eye and the intelligence.

questions.question: What does the changing battlefield teach about life in this world?
questions.answer: It teaches that life here is unstable and always changing.

questions.question: Why might a person feel worried after noticing this change?
questions.answer: Because he sees that things he loves may disappear.

questions.question: What better path is announced by the Qur’an?
questions.answer: The path of giving the trust back to Allah.

questions.question: What makes this path different from simply holding onto worldly things?
questions.answer: It turns something temporary into something lasting and rewarding.

questions.question: What number of profits is clearly promised in the passage?
questions.answer: Five.
